_doc: THE ONE PIN of the gix (gitoxide) binary libs:gix ships (#646). build.gradle reads this file, downloads each ABI's official release tarball ONCE into build/, refuses on a sha256 mismatch of the tarball AND of the extracted binary (the #288 / #348 fetch-once-refuse-on-mismatch pattern, as libs:rclone does it), reads the ELF program headers and refuses if PT_INTERP is present, and lands the binary as jniLibs/<abi>/libgix.so. That name is not decoration: on API 29+ an app may not exec a file it wrote into its own data directory (W^X), but it MAY exec what the installer extracted into nativeLibraryDir, and only files named lib*.so get extracted there — which is also why the PACKAGING app must set packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging = true (AGP's default keeps .so files compressed inside the APK and mmaps them, extracting nothing). GixRunner execs applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir + '/libgix.so'.
_doc_why_not_canonical_git: MEASURED 2026-09-29 (a0_docs/eng-specs/terminal-per-tool-libs-measurement.md §1-§3): canonical git CANNOT ship this way. `git-remote-https` is a SEPARATE EXECUTABLE — not a builtin, not a symlink to git — so HTTPS transport needs a second file under that literal name, and Android extracts only lib*.so. Without it git fails loudly (`git: 'remote-https' is not a git command`, exit 128). Canonical git is also glibc-dynamic (PT_INTERP present) and no credible static aarch64-musl canonical-git prebuilt exists to pin — both searched and reported as measured negatives. gitoxide is the one real single-file git: HTTPS transport is built in (rustls, the `max-pure` flavour, which is what makes it fully static), and it needs no helper process at all.
_doc_interp: MEASURED, INDEPENDENTLY RE-MEASURED FOR THIS PIN 2026-09-29. arm64: NO PT_INTERP and NO PT_DYNAMIC — fully static, the exact rclone property. x86_64: NO PT_INTERP but PT_DYNAMIC IS PRESENT — that is a static-PIE (a dynamic section for self-relocation, no interpreter requested), which the kernel still runs directly. The guard below refuses PT_INTERP and only PT_INTERP, because PT_INTERP is the header that actually decides whether a loader must exist on the filesystem; a static-PIE has no such dependency. This is recorded because the eng-spec stated 'no PT_INTERP and no PT_DYNAMIC' as one property and for the x86_64 build only the first half holds — the pin must not claim more than was measured. Android x86_64 is emulator-only here; arm64 is the device.
_doc_proof_on_device: RUN ON THE REAL PHONE, not documented: renamed to libgix.so and invoked as `env -i PATH=/nonexistent HOME=/nonexistent ./libgix.so clone --depth 1 https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide.git gx`, it EXITED 0 with a valid .git present. Its three child execs (tput cols, tput lines, `git config -lz …`) ALL failed ENOENT against /nonexistent and the clone succeeded anyway: tput is cosmetic terminal sizing and the git-config probe is gitoxide reading an installed git's config for compatibility, both optional. `fetch` works the same way. So one file, HTTPS transport built in, zero REQUIRED helpers, 17.9 MB.
_doc_no_push: gix HAS NO PUSH, and nothing here pretends otherwise: `gix push` answers `error: unrecognized subcommand 'push'` (measured). This library therefore declares `verbs` below as clone and fetch ONLY, GixRunner refuses any other verb, and #646's guard fails the build if push is ever routed here. Push belongs to the terminal handoff (#642's RUN_COMMAND, shipped at 74225166b) or to JGit where it already works.
